meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'again', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'покоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry', paired with 'забеспокоиться'.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Очень приятно. А в чём дело?
examples.trans: Pleased to meet you. So what's the matter?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'against', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Все в городе хотят этот кластер. Только ты против.
examples.trans: Everyone in town wants this cluster. Only you are against it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'what; what a', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'aroma; scent' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я просто хотел добавить яркий аромат.
examples.trans: I simply wanted to add a vivid aroma.

examples.text: А почему они тогда в старом здании? Осипенко сказал, что деньги забрал ты!
examples.trans: Then why are they in the old building? Osipenko said that you took the money!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лшебник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'wizard, magician' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В этой сказке живёт добрый волшебник.
examples.trans: A kind wizard lives in this fairy tale.
You know, Danya is simply a wizard! Thank you!

стараться.gloss: to try, to make an effort

meanings.en: to try, to make an effort
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тараться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to try, to make an effort', paired with 'постараться'.

examples.trans: He always tries to help his friends.

examples.text: Марина, зря вы стараетесь. Он никогда не уйдёт от своей Аллы Евгеньевны.
examples.trans: Marina, you're trying in vain. He will never leave his Alla Evgenyevna.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пециально'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Are you doing this on purpose?
Are you doing this on purpose or what?
You left it here on purpose.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello, hi', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vika, I am really hungry for something.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'адиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sit down', paired with 'сесть'.

related.gloss: not to to sit down (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'uh-huh, yeah', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yeah, right, like with the Cayenne?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лава'). Common feminine noun meaning 'glory, fame' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.

examples.text: Слава богу! Я пьяных за рулём просто терпеть не могу!
examples.trans: Thank goodness! I simply cannot stand drunk people behind the wheel!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
